payload.analysis:
To design a diversified portfolio that meets the client's risk profile, I recommend a mix of moderate-growth equity investments, income-generating bond holdings, and low-volatility commodity exposure. To achieve this, we will allocate 60% to equities, 30% to fixed-income securities, and 10% to commodities. Here's a proposed maturity ladder for the bond holdings, based on a laddered structure: 40% in a short-term government bond (maturity years = 2), 20% in an intermediate-term corporate bond (maturity years = 5), and 30% in a long-term municipal bond (maturity years = 10). The commodity allocation will be divided equally across gold, oil, and agriculture. We must carefully consider these allocations to ensure they do not increase overall portfolio duration above 7 years.

Laddered maturity structure: our recommended bond holding ages are staggered over several years, minimizing the risk of liquidity drought in any given period. Specifically, we're spreading out maturities so that no more than 30% of bonds mature in a single year.
